  MINUTES
  VERNON CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  TUESDAY, JULY 7, 2026
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4305 SANTA FE AVENUE

  CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ybarra called the meeting to order at 9:01 a.m.

  FLAG SALUTE
  Mayor Ybarra led the Flag Salute.

  ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:
  Melissa Ybarra, Mayor
  Jesus Rivera, Mayor Pro Tem
  Crystal Larios, Council Member
  Judith Merlo, Council Member
  Monica Rodriguez, Council Member

  STAFF PRESENT:
  Brian Saeki, City Administrator
  Zaynah Moussa-Milward, City Attorney
  Genoveva Rocha, City Clerk
  Alice Hui, Finance Director/City Treasurer
  Vernoica Petrosyan, Health and Environmental Control Director
  Lisette Grizzelle, Human Resources Manager
  Robert Sousa, Police Chief
  Dan Wall, Public Works Director-City Engineer
  Todd Dusenberry, Public Utilities General Manager

  APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The question was called and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  PUBLIC COMMENT
  None.
 Docusign Envelope ID: E6DAC28B-FBEF-81F7-82D8-0B9DD27AB908

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 2 of 6
  July 7, 2026

  PRESENTATIONS

  1.  Recognition of Outgoing City Commission and Committee Members
  Recommendation: Present Certificates of Recognition to outgoing Business and
  Industry Commission Members Thomas Condon, Hector Morfin, and Navdeep
  (Duncan) Sachdeva; Green Vernon Commission Member Jackelyne (Jacquie)
  Cabrera; Vernon CommUNITY Fund Grant Committee Member Sebastian Lozano;
  and Vernon Housing Commission Member Leticia Lopez.

  City Clerk, Genoveva Rocha presented the staff report. Mayor Ybarra presented a
  Certificate of Recognition to Duncan Sachdeva and Leticia Lopez who were the
  members that were present.

  2.  Proclamation Recognizing Retiring Employee - Jose Zermeno
  Recommendation: Acknowledge and present a proclamation to retiring employee
  Jose Zermeno, Street Maintenance Worker, in recognition of his dedicated service
  to the City of Vernon.

  Director of Public Works, Dan Wall presented the staff report. Mayor Ybarra
  presented the proclamation to Jose Zermeno.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra, asked if
  any member wished to pull any item. Council Member Larios indicated that she
  would be abstaining from voting on Item No. 11 due to personal conflict. Mayor
  Ybarra called for a motion to approve the consent calendar.

  MOTION
  Council Member Merlo moved and Mayor Pro Tem Rivera seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar with the exception of Item No. 11. The question
  was called and the motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  3.  Meeting Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the June 16, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
  Minutes.
  4.  Claims Against the City
  Recommendation: Receive and file the claim submitted by Giovanna Silvestre.
  5.  Operating Account Warrant Register
  Recommendation: Approve Operating Account Warrant Register No. 176, for the
  period of May 17, 2026 through May 30, 2026, totaling $8,312,139.04 and
  consisting of ratification of electronic payments totaling $8,187,243.81 and
  ratification of the issuance of early checks totaling $124,895.23.
  6.  Public Works Department Monthly Report
  Recommendation: Receive and file the May 2026 Building Report.
 Docusign Envelope ID: E6DAC28B-FBEF-81F7-82D8-0B9DD27AB908

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 3 of 6
  July 7, 2026

  7.  Report on Contract Award to Arise Incorporated Approved by the City
  Administrator
  Recommendation: Receive and file a report on the award of Amendment No. 1 and
  Statement of Work No. 2 for the Services Agreement with Arise Incorporated for
  boiler and pressure vessel inspection services at the Malburg Generating Station
  for an amount not-to-exceed $4,790, as approved by the City Administrator
  pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Section 3.32.110(B)(2).
  8.  Report on Contract Award to Tetra Tech, Inc. Approved by the City
  Administrator
  Recommendation: Receive and file the report on the award of a Professional
  Services Agreement to Tetra Tech Inc., for a five-year term to conduct vapor
  monitoring and sampling services of the Former Thermador Site for a not-to-
  exceed cost of $96,429, as approved by the City Administrator pursuant to Vernon
  Municipal Code Sections 3.32.110(B)(2) and 3.32.220(B).
  9.  Professional Services Agreement with Shuster Advisory Group for Financial
  Advisory Consulting Services
  Recommendation: Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute a
  Professional Services Agreement with Shuster Advisory Group, in substantially the
  same form as submitted, for Financial Advisory Consulting Services for a total
  amount not-to-exceed $90,000, for a 3-year term.
  10.  Appointments to the Los Angeles Gateway Region Integrated Water
  Management Joint Power Authority (GWMA)
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. 2026-035 updating the City staff
  appointments to the GWMA and repealing Resolution No. 2025-002.
  12.  Notice of Completion for Contract No. 20260102 - West Wing HVAC
  Replacement
  Recommendation:
  A. Find that the proposed action is categorically exempt from California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review, in accordance with CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15301, because the project consists of a full replacement of the existing
  HVAC main unit on the West Wing of the City Hall Structure and involves negligible
  or no expansion of an existing use;
  B. Accept the work of Western Allied Corporation as related to City Contract No.
  20260102; and
  C. Authorize the Director of Public Works to execute and submit the Notice of
  Completion for the project to the Los Angeles County Recorder’s Office.
 Docusign Envelope ID: E6DAC28B-FBEF-81F7-82D8-0B9DD27AB908

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 4 of 6
  July 7, 2026

  13.  Purchase Order with National Auto Fleet Group
  Recommendation:
  A. Approve and authorize the issuance of a Purchase Order with National Auto
  Fleet Group (NAFG) for a 2026 Chevrolet Silverado EV for a total amount not-to-
  exceed $62,460.85;
  B. Authorize a contingency amount of ten percent (10%) or $6,246.09 for the
  vehicle purchase from NAFG in case of unforeseen fluctuations in price by inflation
  or supply chain issues; and
  C. Authorize the City Administrator to facilitate the bidding and purchase of a
  comparable vehicle for an amount not-to-exceed $68,706.94 (NAFG price plus
  contingency amount) from an alternate source/dealership should NAFG vehicle
  availability be impacted by inventory shortages.

  The following Item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for individual
  consideration.:

  11.  Memorandum of Understanding with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan
  Transportation Authority
  Recommendation:
  A. Find that the approval of the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) proposed
  in this staff report is exempt under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  in accordance with CEQA Guidelines Section 15303, because the project consists
  of new construction of limited small new facilities;
  B. Find that pursuant to California Public Resources Code (PRC) Section
  21080.25(a)(11), Transportation Prioritization Projects include, but are not limited
  to: (E) "transit stop access and safety improvements, including, but not limited to,
  the installation of bus shelters, lighting, transit bulbs, and the installation of transit
  boarding landings and islands" and pursuant to PRC Section 21080.25(b)(3),
  Transit Prioritization Projects are statutorily exempt from CEQA; and
  C. Authorize the City Administrator to execute the MOU for the Metro Southeast
  Los Angeles Transit Improvements Projects (SELA TIP) between the City of
  Vernon (City) and the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
  (LACMTA or Metro), in substantially the same form as submitted herewith. The
  MOU would authorize the LACMTA to reimburse the City for the installation of new
  bus shelters and amenities at ten (10) Metro bus stop locations within the City's
  boundaries.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve Item No. 11. The question was called and the motion carried with 4
  members voting in favor, 0 voting in opposition and Council Member Larios
  abstaining.

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 5 of 6
  July 7, 2026

  NEW BUSINESS

  14.  Confirmation Letter with NRG Business Marketing LLC
  Recommendation:
  A. Find the action is not in reference to a “project” subject to the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Guidelines Section 15378 because it
  involves the continuing administrative activity of purchasing power and resource
  adequacy; and even if it were a “project” subject to CEQA, the approval requested
  is exempt in accordance with CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), the general
  rule that CEQA only applies to projects that may have a significant effect on the
  environment, and any construction that may occur by a private party in the future
  in reliance on this approval would be subject to CEQA review by another
  governmental agency at the time when actual details of any physical proposal
  would be more than speculative; and
  B. Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute the Confirmation Letter
  with NRG Business Marketing LLC, in substantially the same form as submitted,
  for the Purchase of Portfolio Content Category Product 1 (PCC1) Energy in the
  amount-not-to exceed $37,000,000 for a 10-year term.

  Public Utilities General Manager Dusenberry presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra called
  for a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Merlo moved and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  15.  City-wide Strategic Plan
  Recommendation:
  Receive a presentation and adopt the City-wide Strategic Plan.

  City Administrator Saeki presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra called
  for a motion

  MOTION
  Council Member Merlo moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to adopt the city-wide strategic plan. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 6 of 6
  July 7, 2026

  ORAL REPORTS
  16.  City Administrator Reports on Activities and Other Announcements

  City Administrator Saeki announced that the city’s business phone lines were
  experiencing service interruptions, but that all 911 emergency lines remained
  operational. He provided alternate non-emergency phone numbers for City Hall
  and the Police Department and informed that the alternate numbers had been
  posted on the City’s website and social media accounts. He also announced the
  opening of the enrollment period for Vernon City Elementary beginning July 20,
  2026, and promoted National Night Out on August 4, 2026.
  17.  Council Reports on Activities (including AB 1234), Announcements, or
  Directives to Staff
  None.
  CLOSED SESSION
  At 9:33 a.m., Mayor Ybarra recessed the meeting to Closed Session
  18.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation (1 potential matter)
  19.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation
  Initiation of Litigation
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Number of potential cases: 1
  RECONVENE
  At 10:24 a.m., Mayor Ybarra adjourned the Closed Session and reconvened the
  regular meeting.
  CLOSED SESSION REPORT
  City Attorney Moussa-Milward reported that the City Council met in Closed
  Session, discussed the items on the agenda, and took no reportable action.
  ADJOURNMENT
  Mayor Ybarra adjourned the meeting at 10:25 a.m.

  _____________________________
